newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Unmerged Swedish banks rise on Norwegian merger.
newsitem.headline: Unmerged Swedish banks rise on Norwegian merger.

text.p: Shares in Swedish banks unaffected by recent restructuring bucked negative trends and rose on the Stockholm exchange on Wednesday, fuelled by the merger between Norway's Christiania Bank and insurer Storebrand.
S-E-Banken rose 1.5 crowns to 79.5, Nordbanken gained one to 253 and JP Bank advanced 0.2 crowns to 36.2. Meanwhile, the exchange's general index was down 1.30 percent at 2,596.92.
"Such a thing (the Norwegian merger) rekindles interest again, the market is reminded that the restructuring of the financial markets is not finished," a trader said.
But no new rumours about an expected merger between Nordbanken and S-E-Banken have surfaced, dealers said.

The two broke off merger talks earlier this year, but Nordbanken has expressed interest in new talks and S-E-Banken will get a new chief executive, Jacob Wallenberg, shortly, so analysts expect a new courtship.
